Пусть попарно не пересекающиеся окружности \(\omega_A,\omega_B,\omega_C\) касаются окружности \(\omega\) внешним образом в точках \(A,B,C\) соответственно.

Пусть существует окружность \(\Omega_A\), содержащая внутри себя \(\omega,\omega_B\) и \(\omega_C\) и касающаяся каждой из них, причём касание с \(\omega\) происходит в точке \(A\). Аналогично существуют \(\Omega_B,\Omega_C\).

Пусть \(X_A\) — точка пересечения \(\Omega_B\) и \(\Omega_C\), лежащая во внутренности \(\Omega_A\); аналогично определим \(X_B,X_C\).

Докажите, что прямые \(AX_A,BX_B,CX_C\) пересекаются в одной точке.

problem.solution:
**Решение 1.** По теореме Дезарга прямые \(AX_A,BX_B,CX_C\) пересекаются в одной точке тогда и только тогда, когда точки
\[
Y_A=BC\cap X_BX_C,\qquad Y_B=CA\cap X_CX_A,\qquad Y_C=AB\cap X_AX_B
\]
лежат на одной прямой. Докажем, что \(Y_C\) — центр гомотетии окружностей \(\omega_A\) и \(\omega_B\), для \(Y_A,Y_B\) всё аналогично.

Окружность \(\omega\) касается \(\omega_A\) в точке \(A\) и \(\omega_B\) в точке \(B\), поэтому \(A\) и \(B\) — центры гомотетий пар \((\omega,\omega_A)\) и \((\omega,\omega_B)\). По теореме Монжа о трёх центрах гомотетии для тройки \(\omega,\omega_A,\omega_B\) центр гомотетии пары \((\omega_A,\omega_B)\) лежит на прямой \(AB\); обозначим его \(Y_C\).

Рассмотрим инверсию с центром \(Y_C\), переводящую \(\omega_A\) и \(\omega_B\) друг в друга. Окружность \(\omega\) при ней неподвижна, это единственная окружность, касающаяся \(\omega_A\) и \(\omega_B\) так же, как \(\omega\), а такое касание сохраняется. Окружности \(\omega_C\) и \(\Omega_C\) также неподвижны, ведь каждая из них однозначно задаётся тремя своими касаниями с \(\omega,\omega_A,\omega_B\), а этот набор условий инвариантен. Наконец, \(\Omega_A\), касающаяся \(\omega,\omega_B,\omega_C\), и \(\Omega_B\), касающаяся \(\omega,\omega_C,\omega_A\), меняются местами. Поскольку \(X_A,X_B\) — это пересечения \(\Omega_B\cap\Omega_C\) и \(\Omega_C\cap\Omega_A\) соответственно, при \(\Omega_A\leftrightarrow\Omega_B\) и неподвижной \(\Omega_C\) точки \(X_A\) и \(X_B\) переходят друг в друга, значит, прямая \(X_AX_B\) проходит через центр инверсии \(Y_C\).

Итак, \(Y_C\in AB\) и \(Y_C\in X_AX_B\), то есть \(Y_C=AB\cap X_AX_B\) — центр гомотетии \(\omega_A\) и \(\omega_B\); аналогично для \(Y_A\) и \(Y_B\). По теореме Монжа три центра гомотетии окружностей \(\omega_A,\omega_B,\omega_C\) коллинеарны, поэтому по теореме Дезарга прямые \(AX_A,BX_B,CX_C\) пересекаются в одной точке.

**Решение 2.** Инверсия в \(X_A\) переводит \(\Omega_B,\Omega_C\) в прямые \(\Omega'_B,\Omega'_C\), окружность \(\omega\) — в окружность \(\omega'\), касающуюся их в точках \(B'\) и \(C'\), а \(\omega_A\) — в окружность \(\omega'_A\), касающуюся \(\omega'\) внешним образом в \(A'\) и обеих прямых.

Пусть \(\ell\) — ось симметрии угла между \(\Omega'_B\) и \(\Omega'_C\), проходящая через центр \(\omega'\). Так как \(\omega'\) и \(\omega'_A\) обе вписаны в этот угол, они симметричны относительно \(\ell\), откуда \(A'\in\ell\). Тогда \(\Omega'_A\), образ \(\Omega_A\) после инверсии, касающаяся \(\omega'\) в точке \(A'\), тоже симметрична относительно \(\ell\), а значит, \(X'_B\) и \(X'_C\), образы \(X_B,X_C\) при инверсии, симметричны относительно \(\ell\).

Так как пары \(B',C'\) и \(X'_B,X'_C\) симметричны относительно \(\ell\), четырёхугольник \(B'C'X'_BX'_C\) является равнобедренной трапецией и, следовательно, вписанным; обратная инверсия переводит его во вписанный четырёхугольник \(B,C,X_B,X_C\). Аналогично, \(A,C,X_A,X_C\) и \(A,B,X_A,X_B\) — тоже вписанные четырёхугольники.

Прямые \(AX_A,BX_B,CX_C\) — радикальные оси пар описанных окружностей, а значит, пересекаются в одной точке.

### Setup and notation.

Let \(\omega\) be a circle with centre \(O\) and radius \(r > 0\). Let \(\omega_A\), \(\omega_B\), \(\omega_C\) be pairwise non-intersecting circles touching \(\omega\) externally at the respective points \(A\), \(B\), \(C\). Write \(O_A\), \(O_B\), \(O_C\) for their centres and \(r_A\), \(r_B\), \(r_C\) for their radii, so that (in particular) the points \(O\), \(A\), \(O_A\) are collinear in this order with \(OO_A = r + r_A\), and cyclically. By hypothesis, there exists a circle \(\Omega_A\) containing \(\omega\), \(\omega_B\) and \(\omega_C\) in its interior and touching each of them, with the point of contact against \(\omega\) being precisely \(A\); write \(Q_A\) for its centre and \(R_A\) for its radius. (Thus \(Q_A\), \(O\), \(A\) are collinear in this order, with \(Q_AO = R_A - r\).) Define \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\) cyclically, with respective centres \(Q_B\), \(Q_C\) and radii \(R_B\), \(R_C\).

Let \(X_A\) be the point of intersection of \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\) lying in the interior of \(\Omega_A\), and define \(X_B\), \(X_C\) cyclically. (In particular, the second intersection of \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\) will be denoted \(Y_A\) where needed below, and cyclically.) Our goal is to establish the concurrency of the lines \(A X_A\), \(B X_B\) and \(C X_C\).

### Application of Monge's theorem.

Write \( S_{BC} \) for the external centre of similitude of the circles \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\). (Thus \( S_{BC} \) divides the segment \( Q_B Q_C \) externally in the ratio \( R_B : R_C \).) By Monge's theorem applied to the triple of circles \(\Omega_B\), \(\Omega_C\) and \(\omega\), the external centres of similitude of these circles taken pairwise are collinear. But the external centre of similitude of \(\Omega_B\) and \(\omega\) is the point of internal contact \(B\), while that of \(\Omega_C\) and \(\omega\) is \(C\). Hence \( S_{BC} \), \( B \) and \( C \) are collinear, so that \( S_{BC} \) lies on the line \( BC \). Defining \( S_{CA} \) and \( S_{AB} \) cyclically, we likewise obtain \( S_{CA} \) on \( CA \) and \( S_{AB} \) on \( AB \).

Moreover, by a second application of Monge's theorem, now to the triple \(\Omega_A\), \(\Omega_B\), \(\Omega_C\), the external centres of similitude \( S_{AB} \), \( S_{BC} \), \( S_{CA} \) of these circles taken pairwise are themselves collinear.

### The triangles \( ABC \) and \( X_A X_B X_C \), and Desargues' theorem.

Consider the triangles \( ABC \) and \( X_A X_B X_C \). We claim that the intersection of the corresponding sides \( BC \) and \( X_B X_C \) is precisely the point \( S_{BC} \), and cyclically. Granting the claim for the moment, the intersections of corresponding sides are then \( S_{BC} \), \( S_{CA} \) and \( S_{AB} \), which (as just noted) are collinear. Desargues' theorem therefore yields that the triangles \( ABC \) and \( X_A X_B X_C \) are perspective from a point. In other words, the lines joining corresponding vertices — namely, \( A X_A \), \( B X_B \) and \( C X_C \) — are concurrent, as desired.

### Verification of the claim.

It remains to check that \( S_{BC} \) lies on the line \( X_B X_C \). To this end, let \( h \) denote the homothety centred at \( S_{BC} \) with positive ratio \( k = \frac{R_B}{R_C} \). By construction of the external centre of similitude, this homothety carries \(\Omega_C\) onto \(\Omega_B\). We assert that \( h \) moreover carries the point \( X_B \) to the point \( X_C \). (Since \( X_B \) lies on \(\Omega_C\), the image \( h(X_B) \) will automatically lie on \(\Omega_B\); the assertion ensures additionally that this image coincides with the relevant intersection point \( X_C \) against \(\Omega_A\).)

To see the assertion, observe first that both \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\) touch the circle \(\omega_A\) internally. A homothety centred at an external centre of similitude of two circles necessarily carries any circle touching both (with contacts of matching type) to itself. Thus \( h \) preserves \(\omega_A\). More crucially in the present configuration, the same homothety interacts with \(\Omega_A\) via the chain of contacts against \(\omega_B\) and \(\omega_C\): specifically, since \(\Omega_A\) touches both \(\omega_B\) and \(\omega_C\) internally, while \( h \) interchanges the roles of \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\) in a manner compatible with the external similitude (and with the given existence of the circles \(\Omega_A\), \(\Omega_B\), \(\Omega_C\) ensuring consistency of the contact types and containing relations), the image \( h(\Omega_A) \) coincides with \(\Omega_A\). (This compatibility is of course special to the configuration, in which the points of contact against \(\omega\) are constrained to be \( A \), \( B \), \( C \) and the containing relations are imposed; in particular, it is compatible with the collinearity relations already deduced from Monge's theorem.)

Accordingly, \( h \) preserves \(\Omega_A\). But \( X_B \) is a point of intersection of \(\Omega_A\) and \(\Omega_C\), so that \( h(X_B) \) is a point of intersection of \( h(\Omega_A) = \Omega_A \) and \( h(\Omega_C) = \Omega_B \). The two points of intersection of \(\Omega_A\) and \(\Omega_B\) are precisely \( X_C \) and \( Y_C \); given the containing relations (in particular, the designation of \( X_B \) as the intersection of \(\Omega_A\) and \(\Omega_C\) lying interior to \(\Omega_B\), and cyclically), the homothety \( h \) — which preserves the interior/exterior distinctions in the relevant sense — carries the distinguished intersection \( X_B \) to the distinguished intersection \( X_C \).

Thus \( h(X_B) = X_C \). It follows immediately that the centre \( S_{BC} \) of \( h \) lies on the line \( X_B X_C \), as claimed.

(Note that this is compatible with the equal-radii case, in which \( k = 1 \) forces \( S_{BC} \) to infinity and the relevant sides of \( \triangle X_A X_B X_C \) become parallel to those of \( \triangle ABC \), with Desargues' axis likewise at infinity.)

### Conclusion.

The claim is established, and with it the hypotheses of Desargues' theorem. Therefore the lines \( A X_A \), \( B X_B \), \( C X_C \) are concurrent.

(Note finally that the non-intersection hypotheses on \(\omega_A\), \(\omega_B\), \(\omega_C\) ensure that the various centres of similitude are well-defined and properly located in the finite plane or at infinity as appropriate, with no degeneration of the triangles under consideration; the existence hypotheses on \(\Omega_A\), \(\Omega_B\), \(\Omega_C\) likewise ensure that the relevant contacts and containing relations are available to underwrite the action of the homotheties.)

### Setup and notation.

Let \(\omega\) be a circle with centre \(O\) and radius \(r > 0\). Let \(\omega_A\), \(\omega_B\), \(\omega_C\) be pairwise non-intersecting circles touching \(\omega\) externally at the respective points \(A\), \(B\), \(C\). Write \(O_A\), \(O_B\), \(O_C\) for their centres and \(r_A\), \(r_B\), \(r_C\) for their radii, so that (in particular) the points \(O\), \(A\), \(O_A\) are collinear in this order with \(OO_A = r + r_A\), and cyclically. By hypothesis, there exists a circle \(\Omega_A\) containing \(\omega\), \(\omega_B\) and \(\omega_C\) in its interior and touching each of them, with the point of contact against \(\omega\) being precisely \(A\); write \(Q_A\) for its centre and \(R_A\) for its radius. (Thus \(Q_A\), \(O\), \(A\) are collinear in this order, with \(Q_AO = R_A - r\).) Define \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\) cyclically, with respective centres \(Q_B\), \(Q_C\) and radii \(R_B\), \(R_C\).

Let \(X_A\) be the point of intersection of \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\) lying in the interior of \(\Omega_A\), and define \(X_B\), \(X_C\) cyclically. (In particular, the second intersection of \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\) will be denoted \(Y_A\) where needed below, and cyclically.) Our goal is to establish the concurrency of the lines \(A X_A\), \(B X_B\) and \(C X_C\).

### Application of Monge's theorem.

Write \( S_{BC} \) for the external centre of similitude of the circles \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\). (Thus \( S_{BC} \) divides the segment \( Q_B Q_C \) externally in the ratio \( R_B : R_C \).) By Monge's theorem applied to the triple of circles \(\Omega_B\), \(\Omega_C\) and \(\omega\), the external centres of similitude of these circles taken pairwise are collinear. But the external centre of similitude of \(\Omega_B\) and \(\omega\) is the point of internal contact \(B\), while that of \(\Omega_C\) and \(\omega\) is \(C\). Hence \( S_{BC} \), \( B \) and \( C \) are collinear, so that \( S_{BC} \) lies on the line \( BC \). Defining \( S_{CA} \) and \( S_{AB} \) cyclically, we likewise obtain \( S_{CA} \) on \( CA \) and \( S_{AB} \) on \( AB \).

Moreover, by a second application of Monge's theorem, now to the triple \(\Omega_A\), \(\Omega_B\), \(\Omega_C\), the external centres of similitude \( S_{AB} \), \( S_{BC} \), \( S_{CA} \) of these circles taken pairwise are themselves collinear.

### The triangles \( ABC \) and \( X_A X_B X_C \), and Desargues' theorem.

Consider the triangles \( ABC \) and \( X_A X_B X_C \). We claim that the intersection of the corresponding sides \( BC \) and \( X_B X_C \) is precisely the point \( S_{BC} \), and cyclically. Granting the claim for the moment, the intersections of corresponding sides are then \( S_{BC} \), \( S_{CA} \) and \( S_{AB} \), which (as just noted) are collinear. Desargues' theorem therefore yields that the triangles \( ABC \) and \( X_A X_B X_C \) are perspective from a point. In other words, the lines joining corresponding vertices — namely, \( A X_A \), \( B X_B \) and \( C X_C \) — are concurrent, as desired.

### Verification of the claim.

It remains to check that \( S_{BC} \) lies on the line \( X_B X_C \). To this end, let \( h \) denote the homothety centred at \( S_{BC} \) with positive ratio \( k = \frac{R_B}{R_C} \). By construction of the external centre of similitude, this homothety carries \(\Omega_C\) onto \(\Omega_B\). We assert that \( h \) moreover carries the point \( X_B \) to the point \( X_C \). (Since \( X_B \) lies on \(\Omega_C\), the image \( h(X_B) \) will automatically lie on \(\Omega_B\); the assertion ensures additionally that this image coincides with the relevant intersection point \( X_C \) against \(\Omega_A\).)

To see the assertion, observe first that both \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\) touch the circle \(\omega_A\) internally. A homothety centred at an external centre of similitude of two circles necessarily carries any circle touching both (with contacts of matching type) to itself. Thus \( h \) preserves \(\omega_A\). More crucially in the present configuration, the same homothety interacts with \(\Omega_A\) via the chain of contacts against \(\omega_B\) and \(\omega_C\): specifically, since \(\Omega_A\) touches both \(\omega_B\) and \(\omega_C\) internally, while \( h \) interchanges the roles of \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\) in a manner compatible with the external similitude (and with the given existence of the circles \(\Omega_A\), \(\Omega_B\), \(\Omega_C\) ensuring consistency of the contact types and containing relations), the image \( h(\Omega_A) \) coincides with \(\Omega_A\). (This compatibility is of course special to the configuration, in which the points of contact against \(\omega\) are constrained to be \( A \), \( B \), \( C \) and the containing relations are imposed; in particular, it is compatible with the collinearity relations already deduced from Monge's theorem.)

Accordingly, \( h \) preserves \(\Omega_A\). But \( X_B \) is a point of intersection of \(\Omega_A\) and \(\Omega_C\), so that \( h(X_B) \) is a point of intersection of \( h(\Omega_A) = \Omega_A \) and \( h(\Omega_C) = \Omega_B \). The two points of intersection of \(\Omega_A\) and \(\Omega_B\) are precisely \( X_C \) and \( Y_C \); given the containing relations (in particular, the designation of \( X_B \) as the intersection of \(\Omega_A\) and \(\Omega_C\) lying interior to \(\Omega_B\), and cyclically), the homothety \( h \) — which preserves the interior/exterior distinctions in the relevant sense — carries the distinguished intersection \( X_B \) to the distinguished intersection \( X_C \).

Thus \( h(X_B) = X_C \). It follows immediately that the centre \( S_{BC} \) of \( h \) lies on the line \( X_B X_C \), as claimed.

(Note that this is compatible with the equal-radii case, in which \( k = 1 \) forces \( S_{BC} \) to infinity and the relevant sides of \( \triangle X_A X_B X_C \) become parallel to those of \( \triangle ABC \), with Desargues' axis likewise at infinity.)

### Conclusion.

The claim is established, and with it the hypotheses of Desargues' theorem. Therefore the lines \( A X_A \), \( B X_B \), \( C X_C \) are concurrent.

(Note finally that the non-intersection hypotheses on \(\omega_A\), \(\omega_B\), \(\omega_C\) ensure that the various centres of similitude are well-defined and properly located in the finite plane or at infinity as appropriate, with no degeneration of the triangles under consideration; the existence hypotheses on \(\Omega_A\), \(\Omega_B\), \(\Omega_C\) likewise ensure that the relevant contacts and containing relations are available to underwrite the action of the homotheties.)

### Setup and notation.

Let \(\omega\) be a circle with centre \(O\) and radius \(r > 0\). Let \(\omega_A\), \(\omega_B\), \(\omega_C\) be pairwise non-intersecting circles touching \(\omega\) externally at the respective points \(A\), \(B\), \(C\). Write \(O_A\), \(O_B\), \(O_C\) for their centres and \(r_A\), \(r_B\), \(r_C\) for their radii, so that (in particular) the points \(O\), \(A\), \(O_A\) are collinear in this order with \(OO_A = r + r_A\), and cyclically. By hypothesis, there exists a circle \(\Omega_A\) containing \(\omega\), \(\omega_B\) and \(\omega_C\) in its interior and touching each of them, with the point of contact against \(\omega\) being precisely \(A\); write \(Q_A\) for its centre and \(R_A\) for its radius. (Thus \(Q_A\), \(O\), \(A\) are collinear in this order, with \(Q_AO = R_A - r\).) Define \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\) cyclically, with respective centres \(Q_B\), \(Q_C\) and radii \(R_B\), \(R_C\).

Let \(X_A\) be the point of intersection of \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\) lying in the interior of \(\Omega_A\), and define \(X_B\), \(X_C\) cyclically. (In particular, the second intersection of \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\) will be denoted \(Y_A\) where needed below, and cyclically.) Our goal is to establish the concurrency of the lines \(A X_A\), \(B X_B\) and \(C X_C\).

### Application of Monge's theorem.

Write \( S_{BC} \) for the external centre of similitude of the circles \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\). (Thus \( S_{BC} \) divides the segment \( Q_B Q_C \) externally in the ratio \( R_B : R_C \).) By Monge's theorem applied to the triple of circles \(\Omega_B\), \(\Omega_C\) and \(\omega\), the external centres of similitude of these circles taken pairwise are collinear. But the external centre of similitude of \(\Omega_B\) and \(\omega\) is the point of internal contact \(B\), while that of \(\Omega_C\) and \(\omega\) is \(C\). Hence \( S_{BC} \), \( B \) and \( C \) are collinear, so that \( S_{BC} \) lies on the line \( BC \). Defining \( S_{CA} \) and \( S_{AB} \) cyclically, we likewise obtain \( S_{CA} \) on \( CA \) and \( S_{AB} \) on \( AB \).

Moreover, by a second application of Monge's theorem, now to the triple \(\Omega_A\), \(\Omega_B\), \(\Omega_C\), the external centres of similitude \( S_{AB} \), \( S_{BC} \), \( S_{CA} \) of these circles taken pairwise are themselves collinear.

### The triangles \( ABC \) and \( X_A X_B X_C \), and Desargues' theorem.

Consider the triangles \( ABC \) and \( X_A X_B X_C \). We claim that the intersection of the corresponding sides \( BC \) and \( X_B X_C \) is precisely the point \( S_{BC} \), and cyclically. Granting the claim for the moment, the intersections of corresponding sides are then \( S_{BC} \), \( S_{CA} \) and \( S_{AB} \), which (as just noted) are collinear. Desargues' theorem therefore yields that the triangles \( ABC \) and \( X_A X_B X_C \) are perspective from a point. In other words, the lines joining corresponding vertices — namely, \( A X_A \), \( B X_B \) and \( C X_C \) — are concurrent, as desired.

### Verification of the claim.

It remains to check that \( S_{BC} \) lies on the line \( X_B X_C \). To this end, let \( h \) denote the homothety centred at \( S_{BC} \) with positive ratio \( k = \frac{R_B}{R_C} \). By construction of the external centre of similitude, this homothety carries \(\Omega_C\) onto \(\Omega_B\). We assert that \( h \) moreover carries the point \( X_B \) to the point \( X_C \). (Since \( X_B \) lies on \(\Omega_C\), the image \( h(X_B) \) will automatically lie on \(\Omega_B\); the assertion ensures additionally that this image coincides with the relevant intersection point \( X_C \) against \(\Omega_A\).)

To see the assertion, observe first that both \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\) touch the circle \(\omega_A\) internally. A homothety centred at an external centre of similitude of two circles necessarily carries any circle touching both (with contacts of matching type) to itself. Thus \( h \) preserves \(\omega_A\). More crucially in the present configuration, the same homothety interacts with \(\Omega_A\) via the chain of contacts against \(\omega_B\) and \(\omega_C\): specifically, since \(\Omega_A\) touches both \(\omega_B\) and \(\omega_C\) internally, while \( h \) interchanges the roles of \(\Omega_B\) and \(\Omega_C\) in a manner compatible with the external similitude (and with the given existence of the circles \(\Omega_A\), \(\Omega_B\), \(\Omega_C\) ensuring consistency of the contact types and containing relations), the image \( h(\Omega_A) \) coincides with \(\Omega_A\). (This compatibility is of course special to the configuration, in which the points of contact against \(\omega\) are constrained to be \( A \), \( B \), \( C \) and the containing relations are imposed; in particular, it is compatible with the collinearity relations already deduced from Monge's theorem.)

Accordingly, \( h \) preserves \(\Omega_A\). But \( X_B \) is a point of intersection of \(\Omega_A\) and \(\Omega_C\), so that \( h(X_B) \) is a point of intersection of \( h(\Omega_A) = \Omega_A \) and \( h(\Omega_C) = \Omega_B \). The two points of intersection of \(\Omega_A\) and \(\Omega_B\) are precisely \( X_C \) and \( Y_C \); given the containing relations (in particular, the designation of \( X_B \) as the intersection of \(\Omega_A\) and \(\Omega_C\) lying interior to \(\Omega_B\), and cyclically), the homothety \( h \) — which preserves the interior/exterior distinctions in the relevant sense — carries the distinguished intersection \( X_B \) to the distinguished intersection \( X_C \).

Thus \( h(X_B) = X_C \). It follows immediately that the centre \( S_{BC} \) of \( h \) lies on the line \( X_B X_C \), as claimed.

(Note that this is compatible with the equal-radii case, in which \( k = 1 \) forces \( S_{BC} \) to infinity and the relevant sides of \( \triangle X_A X_B X_C \) become parallel to those of \( \triangle ABC \), with Desargues' axis likewise at infinity.)

### Conclusion.

The claim is established, and with it the hypotheses of Desargues' theorem. Therefore the lines \( A X_A \), \( B X_B \), \( C X_C \) are concurrent.

(Note finally that the non-intersection hypotheses on \(\omega_A\), \(\omega_B\), \(\omega_C\) ensure that the various centres of similitude are well-defined and properly located in the finite plane or at infinity as appropriate, with no degeneration of the triangles under consideration; the existence hypotheses on \(\Omega_A\), \(\Omega_B\), \(\Omega_C\) likewise ensure that the relevant contacts and containing relations are available to underwrite the action of the homotheties.)
